scope.primaryPopulation: All distinct class/ER declarations and relationship endpoints in the nine original model-diagram files, counted once per service. Supplemental named report constructs are separate and do not change this denominator.
scope.supplementaryPopulation: Selected explicitly named supporting report dictionary/structure concepts needed to assess meaning. This is not an exhaustive AWS SDK response/request-type census.
scope.coverageInterpretation: NORMALIZED means a reachable typed core representation exists for the construct and preserves its essential role; it does not claim every native field is normalized or that an adapter is implemented. RETAINED_ONLY means a named Source profile or retained evidence preserves content without a normalized domain binding. PARTIAL means some typed structure exists or a mapped normalization is claimed but an identified essential semantic binding is missing. UNMAPPED means no accountable representation is found.
scope.entityDeclarationWarning: An ER/class box is counted as a source construct, not automatically as an independently managed AWS resource or as a target entity.
scope.sourceSemanticKindNote: NATIVE_RESOURCE denotes a provider-identified domain object in these analyses, including a scoped Health impact or catalog type. It is not a claim that each supports independent AWS CRUD. APPLICATION_ENTITY includes locally identified captures, observations and catalog rows; relationship/value/history/view boxes are reported separately.

constructs.previousUse: The stable event identity tied event type, service, scope and impacted geography together without multiplying it by account context or notification delivery.

constructs.coverageReason: HealthEvent provides a scoped canonical identity, provider ARN and typed classification/index fields with an exact selected Source. Provider detail fields remain retained evidence rather than additional event identities.

constructs.identity: Provider type code qualified by service/source scope.
constructs.coverageReason: A named EventType source profile retains the catalog payload. There is no bound normalized EventType value or entity; inspect the retained source when this catalog breadth is needed.

constructs.declarationReason: Declared as a named ER/class construct in the original diagram; that notation does not imply an independent AWS resource or a required target entity.

constructs.identity: Scoped native policy ARN.
constructs.coverageReason: The policy entity retains native identity, selected evidence and owner-versioned component values. Detailed metric constraints are assessed separately under PolicyComponent.

constructs.declarationReason: Declared as a named ER/class construct in the original diagram; that notation does not imply an independent AWS resource or a required target entity.
constructs.previousUse: Held up to four typed policy families with defined numeric targets, units and disaster-recovery approach.
constructs.identity: Policy + component type; no independent AWS lifecycle.
constructs.coverageReason: ResiliencePolicy.components binds PolicyComponent with a known component family, numeric targets, explicit units and an optional disaster-recovery approach. This represents the source component meaning as an owner-versioned value. The RPC ResiliencePolicyChanges and RecoveryTargetsInput shapes additionally specify native edit metrics and bounds. Open read-map keys and looser metric/unit/integer checks are validation-completeness concerns, not a missing representation.
validationLimitations: The normalized read maps do not themselves constrain which metric keys, units or integer-valued targets belong to each component family. Record or enforce those rules for known metrics while preserving deliberate tolerance of future provider values.

constructs.declarationReason: Declared as a named ER/class construct in the original diagram; that notation does not imply an independent AWS resource or a required target entity.

constructs.coverageReason: Observation supplies a timed occurrence with an exact Source reference, while same-service PolicyContext binds effectiveTargetObservation and effectiveTargetSource. Together they preserve the service-scoped effective-target observation envelope and historical selection without a new observation subtype. The untyped child metric values are assessed separately under EffectiveTarget; they do not make the envelope itself unmapped or partial.

constructs.declarationReason: Declared as a named ER/class construct in the original diagram; that notation does not imply an independent AWS resource or a required target entity.

constructs.coverageReason: Only a retained Source profile describes target entries. No EffectiveTarget schema exists; profile observedFields are prose hints and do not enforce the metric set or provenance.
gaps: The profile calls provenance policyType while the source report distinguishes ownership source SELF/CROSS_ACCOUNT from assignment origin. Reconcile names and typed semantics against the pinned source before normalization.

constructs.coverageReason: Snapshot(kind=POLICY_CONTEXT) enforces PolicyContext with serviceId, exact assignment/effective-target evidence and explicit provider-evaluated-revision knowledge. Capturing evidence does not create a provider revision.

evidence.heading: Reviewed capture identity and detail coverage

constructs.previousUse: Captured a scoped finding enumeration with separate list/detail coverage and an optional same-service assessment correlation plus its basis.
constructs.identity: Local capture ID under Service, with exact query/interval; assessment relation was correlation only.

There is no explicit typed related-assessment plus correlationBasis value; using generic query filters or a generic subject alone would not preserve that qualified relation.
gaps: Declare how optional assessment correlation is encoded and validated under Collection or a typed capture value. Keep it explicitly non-authoritative; do not add an Assessment→Finding ownership foreign key.

findings.title: Localized EventDescription is declared but unbound
findings.recommendation: Bind the existing value to the correct contextual owner/profile if normalized description access is required; otherwise classify it explicitly as retained-only. Do not add a description entity.

findings.title: Health failedSet item scope is absent from normalized errors
findings.recommendation: Represent per-item event/account failure and partial-success outcome through a typed owned collection or registered response shape; keep transport failures separate.

findings.title: OrganizationHealthAccess registry targets omit its actual owner
findings.recommendation: Correct registry target metadata to include Workspace and the OrganizationAccess binding. The model already has the appropriate owned value.

findings.title: Match confidence and lifecycle candidate semantics need an explicit disposition
findings.recommendation: Decide and document whether candidate maps to UNKNOWN and whether confidence is resolved from the rule/evidence or exposed as a small owned value. Avoid claiming exact semantic parity until that rule is explicit.

findings.title: Effective target values remain retained rather than normalized
findings.recommendation: Keep the already normalized service-scoped observation envelope and exact PolicyContext references. Add a typed owned eight-metric value contract, with units and source-policy provenance, bound through the existing Source/profile or capture where normalized target-value access is required. Reconcile policyType versus ownership-source naming; do not infer a policy ARN or inheritance from a label.

findings.title: Policy component read-shape validation can be tightened
findings.recommendation: Retain the existing normalized PolicyComponent owner binding. Document or enforce allowed known metric keys, numeric/integer semantics and unit rules per component family; RPC ResiliencePolicyChanges and RecoveryTargetsInput already provide narrower native edit shapes. This is a validation-completeness finding, not a missing component representation or a reason to create another entity.

findings.title: Finding capture assessment correlation lacks a typed basis
findings.recommendation: Preserve optional same-service related-assessment reference and correlation basis as a small owned capture/query-context value, or explicitly defer this former facade capability.

findings.title: Recommendation identity is normalized but its content is arbitrary JSON
findings.recommendation: Bind ordered suggestedChanges/category content to a typed value when normalized comparison/rendering is required. Retain raw provider evidence for extension and do not create native recommendation IDs.

findings.title: Native topology edge property collections are not normalized
findings.recommendation: Define lossless property expansion/grouping or an owned properties collection carrying native type and optional inferred label. Preserve source grouping and same-snapshot endpoints.

findings.title: Operational event subject linkage remains untyped
findings.recommendation: Bind typed event subjects with role, scoped identity and linkage evidence if the timeline/subject use case is in scope. Native envelope resources alone do not establish those application relationships.

findings.title: Source reference tombstone semantics have no explicit target field
findings.recommendation: Define the minimal deletion/visibility observation and how historical references resolve it; do not add a version-only or tombstone-only entity by default.

findings.title: Runtime-health and component-posture evidence are retained profiles
findings.recommendation: Keep retained evidence coverage separate from typed measurement/component-outcome coverage. Select concrete owned observation schemas from product use cases before claiming normalized signal or component parity.

findings.title: Native administration and auxiliary configuration are intentional retention boundaries
findings.recommendation: Retain these registered native profiles and declare their product normalization/command deferrals explicitly. They do not each justify a new first-class entity.

limitations: Field-by-field AWS SDK compatibility and adapter runtime behavior are outside this audit.
NORMALIZED denotes the typed core representation explained in each row, not universal normalization of every retained provider field.
Supplementary report concepts are a declared supporting sample, not a complete native SDK DTO population.
